paper_title: Quantum Mechanics of Stochastic Systems (Kuang, 2025, arXiv)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\subsection*{Claim}
Let \(P:\mathbb{N}_0\to[0,1]\) satisfy \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)=1\), let
\[
|\psi_P\rangle:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(n)}\,|n\rangle,
\qquad
\hat N|n\rangle=n|n\rangle,
\]
where \(\{|n\rangle:n\in\mathbb{N}_0\}\) is orthonormal.  For every event \(A\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0\), every real function \(f\) with \(\sum_n |f(n)|P(n)<\infty\), and every finite-entropy law, the count-basis representation gives
\[
\langle\psi_P|\psi_P\rangle=1,
\qquad
\langle\psi_P|\Pi_A|\psi_P\rangle=\sum_{n\in A}P(n),
\]
\[
\langle\psi_P|f(\hat N)|\psi_P\rangle=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}f(n)P(n),
\qquad
S(\psi_P)=-\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)\log P(n),
\]
with \(0\log0:=0\) and \(\Pi_A:=\sum_{n\in A}|n\rangle\langle n|\).

\subsection*{Derivation}
The norm is
\begin{align}
\langle\psi_P|\psi_P\rangle
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}e^{-i\theta_m}e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(m)P(n)}\langle m|n\rangle\\
&=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}e^{-i\theta_m}e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(m)P(n)}\delta_{mn}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)=1.
\end{align}
For an event \(A\), since \(\Pi_A|n\rangle=|n\rangle\) when \(n\in A\) and \(\Pi_A|n\rangle=0\) otherwise,
\begin{align}
\langle\psi_P|\Pi_A|\psi_P\rangle
&=\sum_{m,n}e^{-i\theta_m}e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(m)P(n)}\langle m|\Pi_A|n\rangle\\
&=\sum_{n\in A}P(n).
\end{align}
Likewise \(f(\hat N)|n\rangle=f(n)|n\rangle\), and the absolute-convergence assumption permits the diagonal sum:
\begin{align}
\langle\psi_P|f(\hat N)|\psi_P\rangle
&=\sum_{m,n}e^{-i\theta_m}e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(m)P(n)}f(n)\delta_{mn}\\
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}f(n)P(n).
\end{align}
Taking \(f(n)=n^q\) recovers every convergent count moment.  Taking the diagonal entropy functional gives
\begin{align}
S(\psi_P)
&=-\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(n)}|^2\log |e^{i\theta_n}\sqrt{P(n)}|^2\\
&=-\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)\log P(n).
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\text{The count-basis state is a probability-preserving embedding of events, moments, and entropy.}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\subsection*{Claim}
Let \(P_N\) be the Binomial law \(\operatorname{Bin}(N,\lambda/N)\), extended by zero outside \(\{0,\ldots,N\}\), and let \(P\) be the Poisson law with mean \(\lambda>0\).  Define
\[
|\psi_N\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{P_N(k)}|k\rangle,
\qquad
|\psi\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{P(k)}|k\rangle.
\]
If \(\|\,|\psi_N\rangle-|\psi\rangle\,\|\to0\), then every bounded count statistic and every modular residue event also converges.  In particular,
\[
\Pr_{P_N}[K\bmod M=r]\to \Pr_P[K\bmod M=r]
\]
for every fixed \(M\geq2\) and residue \(r\).

\subsection*{Derivation}
Set \(a_k:=\sqrt{P_N(k)}\), \(b_k:=\sqrt{P(k)}\), and
\[
d_N:=\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(a_k-b_k)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The total-variation distance satisfies
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|P_N(k)-P(k)|
&=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|a_k^2-b_k^2|\\
&=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|a_k-b_k||a_k+b_k|\\
&\leq \left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(a_k-b_k)^2\right)^{1/2}
     \left(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(a_k+b_k)^2\right)^{1/2}\\
&\leq 2d_N,
\end{align}
because \(\sum_k a_k^2=\sum_k b_k^2=1\).  Hence
\[
\|P_N-P\|_{TV}:=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|P_N(k)-P(k)|\leq d_N.
\]
For any bounded function \(g\),
\begin{align}
\left|\sum_k g(k)P_N(k)-\sum_k g(k)P(k)\right|
&\leq \|g\|_{\infty}\sum_k|P_N(k)-P(k)|\\
&\leq 2\|g\|_{\infty}d_N\to0.
\end{align}
For a modular residue, take \(g(k)=1\) if \(k\equiv r\pmod M\) and \(g(k)=0\) otherwise.  Then \(\|g\|_{\infty}=1\), so
\begin{align}
\left|\Pr_{P_N}[K\bmod M=r]-\Pr_P[K\bmod M=r]\right|&\leq2d_N\to0.
\end{align}

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\text{Strong Hilbert-space convergence of square-root states implies convergence of bounded observables and modular residues.}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_5:
\subsection*{Claim}
Let \(M\geq2\), \(\theta_\ell:=2\pi\ell/M\), and \(\phi(\theta):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{i\theta n}\).  The residue law \(Q_r:=\Pr[K\bmod M=r]\) is
\[
Q_r=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi(\theta_\ell)e^{-i\theta_\ell r}.
\]
Moreover, for Negative Binomial, Binomial, and Poisson laws, every nonzero Fourier mode has magnitude below one, so
\[
\left|Q_r-\frac{1}{M}\right|\leq \frac{M-1}{M}\rho^m
\]
with \(0<\rho<1\) and \(m=r_0\), \(m=n\), or \(m=\lambda\) for \(NB(r_0,p)\), \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)\), or \(\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), respectively.

\subsection*{Derivation}
The root-of-unity filter gives
\[
\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}e^{i\theta_\ell(n-r)}=\begin{cases}1,&n\equiv r\pmod M,\\0,&n\not\equiv r\pmod M.\end{cases}
\]
Therefore
\begin{align}
Q_r
&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}e^{i\theta_\ell(n-r)}\\
&=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\left(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}P(n)e^{i\theta_\ell n}\right)e^{-i\theta_\ell r}\\
&=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi(\theta_\ell)e^{-i\theta_\ell r}.
\end{align}
Since \(\phi(0)=1\),
\begin{align}
\left|Q_r-\frac{1}{M}\right|
&\leq \frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M-1}|\phi(\theta_\ell)|.
\end{align}
For \(NB(r_0,p)\) with \(0<p<1\),
\begin{align}
\phi_{NB}(\theta)&=\left(\frac{1-p}{1-pe^{i\theta}}\right)^{r_0},\\
|\phi_{NB}(\theta_\ell)|&=\left(\frac{1-p}{|1-pe^{i\theta_\ell}|}\right)^{r_0}.
\end{align}
For \(\ell=1,
\ldots,M-1\), \(|1-pe^{i\theta_\ell}|^2=(1-p)^2+2p(1-\cos\theta_\ell)>(1-p)^2\), hence
\[
\rho_{NB}:=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq M-1}\frac{1-p}{|1-pe^{i\theta_\ell}|}<1.
\]
For \(K\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,p)\),
\begin{align}
\phi_B(\theta)&=(1-p+pe^{i\theta})^n,
\end{align}
so with \(0<p<1\),
\[
\rho_B:=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq M-1}|1-p+pe^{i\theta_\ell}|<1.
\]
For \(K\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\),
\begin{align}
\phi_P(\theta)&=\exp(\lambda(e^{i\theta}-1)),\\
|\phi_P(\theta_\ell)|&=\exp(\lambda(\cos\theta_\ell-1))
=\left(e^{\cos\theta_\ell-1}\right)^\lambda,
\end{align}
and
\[
\rho_P:=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq M-1}e^{\cos\theta_\ell-1}<1.
\]
Substitution into the nonzero-mode bound yields the stated exponential uniformity estimate.

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{Q_r=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}\phi(2\pi\ell/M)e^{-2\pi i\ell r/M},\qquad
|Q_r-1/M|\leq ((M-1)/M)\rho^m.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_6:
\subsection*{Claim}
The probability-engineering strength differs by family in the precise way required by the target goals.  The Poisson member has an explicit displaced-oscillator Hamiltonian eigenstate construction, while Binomial, Negative Binomial/Geometric, and Hypergeometric members have structure-level perturbation certificates: finite-rank support, waiting-time plus correlation weighting, and projection constraints.  Each certificate is sufficient for exact count-basis measurement probabilities.

\subsection*{Derivation}
For Poisson, let
\[
\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}=\hbar\omega\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat a+\frac{1}{2}\right),
\qquad
\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}=\hbar\omega(-\alpha\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat a+|\alpha|^2).
\]
Using \(\hat D(\alpha)\hat a\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)=\hat a-\alpha\) and the corresponding adjoint identity,
\begin{align}
\hat D(\alpha)\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}\hat D^\dagger(\alpha)
&=\hbar\omega\left((\hat a^\dagger-\alpha^*)(\hat a-\alpha)+\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}+\Delta V_{\mathrm{Pois}}
=\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}.
\end{align}
Therefore, for \(|\alpha\rangle=\hat D(\alpha)|0\rangle\),
\begin{align}
\hat H_{\mathrm{Pois}}|\alpha\rangle
&=\hat D(\alpha)\hat H_{\mathrm{QHO}}|0\rangle
=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}|\alpha\rangle.
\end{align}
The coherent-state coefficient computation gives \(|\langle n|\alpha\rangle|^2=e^{-|\alpha|^2}|\alpha|^{2n}/n!\), so \(\lambda=|\alpha|^2\) realizes the Poisson law.

For Binomial, define the finite-support projector
\[
\Pi_{\leq N}:=\sum_{k=0}^{N}|k\rangle\langle k|,
\qquad
|\psi_B\rangle:=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\sqrt{\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}}|k\rangle.
\]
Then \(\Pi_{\leq N}|\psi_B\rangle=|\psi_B\rangle\), \((I-\Pi_{\leq N})|\psi_B\rangle=0\), and
\begin{align}
\langle\psi_B|\,|k\rangle\langle k|\,|\psi_B\rangle
&=\binom{N}{k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k}
\end{align}
for \(0\leq k\leq N\), with zero probability outside the finite-rank sector.

For Negative Binomial, write the zero-based Geometric amplitude as
\[
\alpha^{(G)}_n(p):=\sqrt{(1-p)p^n}.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
\alpha^{(NB)}_n(r,p)
&=\sqrt{\binom{n+r-1}{n}(1-p)^rp^n}\\
&=\sqrt{\binom{n+r-1}{n}}(1-p)^{(r-1)/2}\alpha^{(G)}_n(p).
\end{align}
Thus \(r=1\) removes the correlation factor and gives the Geometric state exactly, while \(r>1\) weights the same waiting-time backbone by the correlation multiplicity \(\binom{n+r-1}{n}\).

For Hypergeometric, define
\[
\Pi_H:=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}|n\rangle\langle n|,
\qquad
|\psi_H\rangle:=\sum_{n=n_-}^{n_+}\sqrt{\frac{\binom{K}{n}\binom{N-K}{M-n}}{\binom{N}{M}}}|n\rangle.
\]
Then \(\Pi_H|\psi_H\rangle=|\psi_H\rangle\), and the count-basis probability is exactly the sampling-without-replacement law on the feasible support.

\subsection*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\text{Poisson is certified by an explicit Hamiltonian eigenstate; the other named laws are certified at the stated structure level.}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
